cases: Reconnect at 1h54 preserves initial ~6h deadline and occurs before 7h TTL.
A later reconnect preserves the most recent successful liveness checkpoint.
Failed send remains due and retries on the next socket keepalive.
Six consecutive failed sends use the existing reconnect backoff and close sockets.
300 idle keepalives cause no extra durable HTTP read and no early liveness.
limits: Successful socket send is not a D1 acknowledgement.
Checkpoint is process-local; a new process begins its existing startup cadence.
No live fleet or multi-tenant soak is claimed.

negative_control.adapter: Clock injection only; baseline liveness logic and per-socket reset unchanged.
